CHIEF COMPLAINT
Recurrent kidney stone, hypertension management, and diabetes follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a female with a history of recurrent kidney stones (approximately 7-8 episodes total). She presented to the emergency room last week with flank pain and was treated with Percocet. She reports the stone has since passed approximately 3 days ago. She denies current hematuria and current pain. She has not seen a urologist in approximately one year.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain or abdominal pain. She reports intermittent insomnia, characterized by worrying at night. She has tried meditation apps which provide some relief. She has tried melatonin a couple of times with minimal benefit.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (diagnosed approximately one year ago), recurrent nephrolithiasis, grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (previously known, unchanged), insomnia.

MEDICATIONS
Amlodipine (Norvasc) 2.5 mg daily, Metformin 500 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports diet includes fast food, cakes, and cookies. She has difficulty controlling diet due to busy schedule and limited time for meal preparation. She sleeps with the television on and keeps her phone by her bedside. She does not regularly check blood glucose at home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood Pressure: 150/90 mmHg at visit. Home blood pressure readings (2-3 times weekly): 130-140/60-70. Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles. Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from prior exam. Abdomen: No tenderness to palpation. Costovertebral angle: No tenderness bilaterally.

RESULTS
A1C: 6.7 (elevated but improved from initial diagnosis).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Nephrolithiasis: Currently passed. Order urinalysis and urine culture. Refer to urology (specifically Dr. Harris) for evaluation of recurrent kidney stones.
Hypertension: Well-controlled on Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. Continue current dose, no changes needed. Provide refills through pharmacy.
Type 2 Diabetes: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Counsel patient to check blood glucose before each meal to guide dietary intake and medication efficacy.
Nutrition: Refer to dietitian for diet counseling with goal of sodium restriction to less than 2300 mg daily to support management of hypertension and diabetes.
Insomnia: Start melatonin 10 mg as needed. Reinforce sleep hygiene measures including turning off electronics, keeping room dark and cool, and enabling sleep mode on phone.
Follow-up appointment in 3 months.
